newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux plan hike in cargo rates in positive mkt.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux plan hike in cargo rates in positive mkt.

text.p: Cargolux plans to increase its ex-Europe cargo rates by between five and ten percent, effective March 1.
Cargolux applied similar increases in October 1996.

"The increases are more or less across-the-board and the scale of them will not differ much from region to region and include South-East Asia, Japan, the U.S. and South America and this reflects the breadth of buoyant demand in the sector," said Pierre Wesner, Cargolux vice-president, Sales and Marketing Europe/ Africa/Middle East told Reuters.
He said North America, traditionally considered to be a weak market, was generating a lot of demand.

Wesner added: "Barring major, unforeseen events, we are probably returning to more stable market conditions and implementing the same scale of rate increases as in the Autumn is already a possibility.

"A fair assessment of the current situation would be that we are perhaps a little short of capacity. Who knows we may have to charter additional aircraft to sees through the peak periods as we have done in the past. However, we're not having to face this problem yet."
He said Cargolux would decide this week on the future size of its fleet.
Earlier this year, the all-cargo airline decided to invest in two, additional Boeing 747-400Fs during the second half of 1997, as opposed to one, as was initially planned.
Cargolux currently operates three 747-400Fs and four 747-200Fs.

"It's probably a little exaggerated to see us with a total of nine aircraft in service but the exact re-composition of the fleet, following the arrival of the two additional 400Fs, should be agreed this week."
Wesner confirmed that Cargolux was banking on 1997 growth in freight tonne kilometres (FTK) to be "well in excess of ten percent" on last year's levels.
The airline flew 2.02 billion FTK in 1996, a rise of four percent on the previous year. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
